findings.evidence: grep for `flavorSymmetry` finds `FlavorSymmetryRelation` only at Symmetries.lean:107 (definition), 465/475 (pion hypotheses) and 487 (existence witness); no lemma relates it to `favored`/`unfavored`.
findings.fix: Add the parallel pair, e.g. `favored_map_of_flavorSymmetryRelation (hρ : Function.Injective ρ) (hv : ∀ h s, Species.map ρ s ∈ valence (τ h) ↔ s ∈ valence h) (hFS : FlavorSymmetryRelation τ ρ D) : favored valence D (τ h) (ρ i) z Q2 = favored valence D h i z Q2`, and likewise for `unfavored`, mirroring lines 319–335.
findings.issue: `FlavorSymmetryRelation` (line 107) is a headline definition with no lemma whose conclusion mentions `favored` or `unfavored`, while `ChargeConjRelation` gets both `favored_conj_of_chargeConjRelation` (319) and `unfavored_conj_of_chargeConjRelation` (329). Its only general consequence is `Invariant.apply_eq_apply`, so a consumer with an isospin-symmetric multiplet must redo the Finset-image argument by hand.

findings.evidence: grep `image_map|map_flavorPair` over EpsilonEridani/ returns no hits; Species.lean:205 has only the `conj` version.
findings.fix: Add `Species.image_map_flavorPair (ρ : Flavor → Flavor') (i : Flavor) : (flavorPair i).image (map ρ) = flavorPair (ρ i)` next to `image_conj_flavorPair`; it needs no injectivity hypothesis since `quark` and `antiquark` are distinct constructors.
findings.issue: `Species` has `image_conj_flavorPair` (the conj action on a flavour pair) but no `map` counterpart, so the flavour-relation lemma above cannot be proved from the public API: `(flavorPair i).image (map ρ) = flavorPair (ρ i)` is absent even though `map_quark`/`map_antiquark`/`map_injective` are all present.

findings.evidence: grep `_pion_` over EpsilonEridani/ lists only `pion_plus`, `pion_zero` and `isValenceFlavor_pion_plus`/`not_isValenceFlavor_pion_zero`; `Pion.valence_minus = {.quark .down, .antiquark .up}` makes both flavours valence flavours of π⁻.
findings.fix: Add `isValenceFlavor_pion_minus` beside `isValenceFlavor_pion_plus` (ValenceContent.lean:296) and the four π⁻ evaluations; each is a one-liner from `favored_eq_apply_quark`/`favored_eq_apply_antiquark` with `(by simp) (by simp)`, exactly as for π⁺.
findings.issue: The worked pion triplet exposes `Pion.valence_minus` (`ValenceContent.lean:271`, `@[simp]`) as public data but states no characteristic lemma for π⁻: there is no `isValenceFlavor_pion_minus` and none of the four `favored_pion_minus_*`/`unfavored_pion_minus_*` evaluations, while π⁺ gets four (425–445) and π⁰ two (449–457). Unconditionally (without assuming `ChargeConjRelation`) a consumer gets nothing about the third member of the multiplet.

summary: The two symmetry relations are presented as co-equal main definitions, but only `ChargeConjRelation` gets consequences stated in terms of `favored`/`unfavored`; `FlavorSymmetryRelation` has none, and the `Species.map`/`flavorPair` lemma needed to state one is missing. The worked pion instance also covers only π⁺ and π⁰.
